To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the inverse probability weighted estimator is a robust approach for estimating the effect of a genetic exposure on a secondary phenotype in a case‐control genetic study.

(i) inverse probability weighted estimating equation analysis of secondary phenotypes in genetic case‐control studies can be more powerful than a full likelihood analysis when the likelihood model is misspecified, and (ii) inverse probability weighted analysis can be more robust to misspecification than likelihood analysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of analyzing the relationship between a genetic exposure and a secondary phenotypic outcome in case‐control studies.
developing and evaluating methods for analyzing data from genetic association studies.
the development of robust methods for the analysis of genetic case‐control studies with secondary phenotypes.
